summary: Verified ENCRYPTION_KEY robustness fix in db._load_fernet. Added tests/test_encryption_key_robustness.py with 4 tests: (a) invalid placeholder 'change-me-to-a-fernet-key' no longer crashes and encrypt/decrypt round-trips, (b) valid Fernet key is used as-is (verified by decrypting with independent Fernet instance), (c) empty ENCRYPTION_KEY still yields working Fernet, (d) arbitrary passphrase derivation is deterministic across reloads. Teardown restores ENCRYPTION_KEY from .env and reloads db so other tests are unaffected. Ran full pytest suite: 17/17 passed in 63.9s (4 new + 13 pre-existing: auth/session, businesses CRUD, node-pairs, demo seed/dashboard, runs/incidents, async compare, invalid incident status, cookie_params http/https/ip/empty, HTTPS Secure;SameSite=None regression on hosted preview). Hosted HTTPS login regression via test_https_cookie_regression confirms POST /api/auth/login admin@driftwatch.io/admin123 returns 200 and GET /api/auth/me returns admin.
critical_code_review_comments: _load_fernet swallows all exceptions from Fernet(...) — fine here because Fernet only raises on invalid key format, but a narrower except (ValueError, binascii.Error) would be marginally cleaner.

Derived-key path uses SHA256 of the raw string as the key material. Deterministic (good for persistence across restarts) but any deployment using a weak passphrase gets a low-entropy key. Consider logging guidance once at startup (already done via WARNING).
Prior finding still stands: auth.cookie_params() only matches lowercase 'https://' prefix; a FRONTEND_URL with uppercase scheme or leading space falls through to non-secure.
seed_data_creation: None new; existing tests use /api/demo/seed and TEST_ prefixed business/node-pair fixtures.
context_for_next_testing_agent: ENCRYPTION_KEY fix fully covered by tests/test_encryption_key_robustness.py. Test module uses load_dotenv() before importing db (db.py reads MONGO_URL at import). Each test sets os.environ['ENCRYPTION_KEY'], importlib.reload(db), asserts round-trip; teardown restores original key and reloads db. All 17 backend tests green.
rca of the issue: Root cause: db.py evaluated Fernet(os.environ['ENCRYPTION_KEY']) at import time. When users deployed with the example .env value 'change-me-to-a-fernet-key' (not a valid urlsafe-b64 32-byte Fernet key), Fernet raised ValueError during module import, so uvicorn/FastAPI failed to boot. The frontend's login POST hit a dead backend, got no JSON body, and displayed the generic 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' Fix: _load_fernet() first tries Fernet(raw_key) as-is; on failure it derives a deterministic valid key via urlsafe_b64encode(sha256(raw_key)) and logs a WARNING. The module now imports cleanly for any string (including empty), so the backend starts and login works; and a real Fernet key is still used verbatim so encrypted secrets remain portable.
